description: The Oregon Statewide Seismic Needs Assessment screened the state's emergency and public buildings for earthquake collapse risk after Senate Bill 2 (2005). DOGAMI field teams applied FEMA 154 rapid visual screening in 2006 to fire stations, acute-care hospitals, police stations, sheriffs' offices, emergency operations centres, public safety answering points, schools and community colleges, and published the results in Open-File Report O-07-02 in 2007. The full spreadsheet is free to download and holds 3,362 building rows with coordinates, year built, structural type, irregularities, soil class, FEMA 154 score modifiers and a collapse potential class from Low to Very High. It includes 650 fire station buildings, 116 hospital buildings, 114 police buildings and 48 sheriff, EOC and dispatch buildings, alongside 2,377 school and college buildings. Site summary reports for each screened site are also available as PDFs on the HazVu pages. Coverage is the state of Oregon, one screening round in 2006. Caveats: rapid visual screening is a coarse method and many structural types were recorded with less than full certainty; the data are not updated after later seismic rehabilitation grants; longitudes are stored as positive degrees west; no licence is stated. Simulation uses: building-level fragility inputs for post-earthquake functionality of fire, police and hospital services in Cascadia scenarios. Related records: California's hospital seismic safety data (data-hcai-california-hospital-seismic-safety-and-construction) cover hospital buildings in the neighbouring state.
